name: Light-space transmittance volumes
definition: A technique where transmittance from a light source is computed once into a 3D grid indexed by position, allowing receivers to look up transmittance via interpolation instead of tracing paths. It is the volume rendering equivalent of deep shadow maps for participating media.
summary: Light-space transmittance volumes pre-calculate optical depth into 3D grids to replace per-receiver ray marching, shifting computation to a single per-cluster grid construction.
